To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electromagnetic and hadron-induced cascades in blazars are distinguishable at the level of ~3σ in the simplest version of the model.

the signatures of the electromagnetic and hadron cascade models are different and can be distinguished from each other at a significance level ~3 σ in the spectra of bright blazars at energies >100 TeV.
the hadronic intergalactica l cascade model can be discriminated from the electromagnetic cascade model at a significance of ~3 σ with current data and at a significance of 6 σ with future CTA data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the search for a cascade component in the spectra of bright blazars using the data of the Fermi Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT), the Cherenkov telescope MAGIC, the Cherenkov telescopes of the High Energy Stereoscopic System (H.E.S.S.), and the Cherenkov Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (VERITAS).
the study of high-energy gamma-ray sources, with a special focus on blazars.
the study of cosmic ray acceleration in the relativistic jets of active galactic nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the cascade component is present, the electromagnetic cascade is the most likely model, but the hadronic cascade cannot be completely ruled out.
the CTA observations of bright blazars can be used to discriminate between the hadronic and electromagnetic intergalactic cascade scenarios.
the electromagnetic cascade is a more likely scenario, although the hadronic cascade can be distinguished at a significance of 3 σ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a secondary component can be detected in blazar spectra at a significance level ~3 σ with CTA, and the secondary component can be used to discriminate between the electromagnetic and hadron models.
the electromagnetic cascade is a viable model for the secondary component of blazar spectra, and the hadronic cascade is a viable alternative.
the electromagnetic model is the best fit to the data, but the hadronic model can be distinguished at a significance level that is not negligible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electromagnetic cascade model can be excluded at a level of ~3σ for a typical observation at the CTA.
the electromagnetic cascade model is not excluded by the existing observations of bright blazars.
the CTA will be able to test the electromagnetic cascade model and the hadronic cascade models in the next decade.
